label: Historical leaders
policy: One deceased historical leader per NationId, favoring civic, liberation, reform, resistance, independence, and nation-building leadership while avoiding genocidal, extremist, and totalitarian avatars. The selector prefers reviewed full-body character art tied to a verified identity portrait, then the portrait, then a named archival cameo.

USA.review_note: His record on race, Indigenous policy, civil liberties, and the limits of emancipation remains historically contested; selection is not blanket moral endorsement.

Swaziland.role: queen regent, land defender, and education leader
Swaziland.rationale: As regent she defended Swazi autonomy and land interests while investing in education and early Swazi print culture.
Swaziland.review_note: A royal and political figure cannot represent every Swazi identity; retain cultural consultation and note that the game's roster uses the historical 1990 name Swaziland.

Paraguay.rationale: He helped restore stability after civil conflict, reorganized public finances, and invested in education and administrative capacity during the 1920s.
Paraguay.review_note: Published sources variously give 1879 or round his birth year to 1880; this proposal follows Paraguayan biographical records using 1879 and should receive local specialist review.

Guyana.rationale: He built a mass anticolonial party, led British Guiana toward self-government, and later returned to office through internationally observed elections.
Guyana.review_note: His Marxist politics and the country's polarized ethnic-party system remain contested; present his anticolonial and electoral record without partisan endorsement.

Suriname.rationale: The educator and former governor became the first president at independence and represented constitutional civilian government until the 1980 military coup.
Suriname.review_note: His office was largely constitutional and independence had many political architects; emphasize his unifying civic role instead of overstating executive power.
